item.title: Survey Finds AI-Generated Code Increases Debugging and Failure Rates and Creates a Comprehension Gap
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/survey-complex-codebases-agents/en/headerimage/agent-friendly-android-cli-1791394744043.jpeg"/><p>A survey conducted by independent research firm Coleman Parkes on behalf of Undo, a company focused on scaling AI-powered root-cause analysis, found that while AI coding agents have accelerated code generation, they have shifted the primary bottleneck to debugging, code comprehension, and maintenance.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: The Async Multiprocessing Has Sound Foundations in Linux, But Further Testing Is Needed
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>At Embedded Linux Conference Europe 2026, Wolfram Sang discussed the Linux building blocks for asymmetric multiprocessing (AMP). He highlighted the solid foundation but noted challenges like limited contributor coverage and fragmented testing. Sang's work on a hardware-spinlock driver revealed maintenance complexities and the need for more reviewers and testers to support evolving AMP systems.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: Grab Redesigns Counter Service Storage for 50% Lower P99 Latency
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/grab-counter-aerospike-migration/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790465865171.jpg"/><p>Grab migrated its high-volume Counter Service from a wide column database to Aerospike using storage abstraction, shadow traffic, data parity validation, and gradual traffic migration. The redesigned data model consolidated time buckets into map-based records. Grab reports about 50% lower production p99 read latency, 1 TB versus 3 TB of disk usage, and 45% to 50% lower cost per node.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: AI in Production: What Breaks, What Works, and Who Approves It? | InfoQ Webinar
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/infoq-ai-webinar/en/headerimage/InfoQ-Webinar-oct-2026-1791382183088.jpg"/><p>On October 14, InfoQ hosts a free 60-minute panel with five practitioners on running AI in production. They'll discuss agent autonomy and human approval, how to verify AI-generated changes, sensitive-data exposure, and production RAG. Registrants can submit questions and will receive the recording.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

item.title: Presentation: The Reinvention of the Dev Team
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/agentic-dev-teams/en/mediumimage/medium-1790242915891.jpeg"/><p>Hannah Foxwell shares how the surge of agentic coding forces engineering leaders to rethink team dynamics. She discusses three key anchors for navigating AI-driven velocity: building software worth building, prioritizing automated safety over speed, and preserving the human element through generalist "broken comb" skillsets and sustainable on-call practices.</p> <i>By Hannah Foxwell</i>

item.title: Article: Building a Session-Ordered Kafka Pipeline in Go
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/apache-kafka-golang-session-ordered-pipeline/en/headerimage/apache-kafka-golang-session-ordered-pipeline-header-1790945957360.jpg"/><p>The article describes a custom implementation that provides a session-level ordering on top of Apache Kafka partitions, supporting strict message ordering across 1000s of independent channels. The solution required application-level routing, consistent hashing, retries, and contiguous watermark commits. Engineers conducted operational hardening supported by extensive performance testing.</p> <i>By Joshua Oluikpe</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Uses an AI Harness to Probe and Harden Its WAF
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-sec-harness/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791312164500.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare placed frontier AI models inside a controlled testing harness to probe its Web Application Firewall (WAF), using blocked attacks as starting points for models to generate and refine new variations.</p> <i>By Matt Foster</i>

item.title: Spanner Omni Reaches GA, Replacing Google's Atomic Clocks and File System with Software
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/spanner-omni-deploy-anywhere-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791038786495.jpg"/><p>Google has made Spanner Omni generally available, running its distributed SQL database on-premises, across clouds or on a laptop. Doing so meant replacing Colossus with a Colossus-like abstraction layer and TrueTime with software-based time synchronization. There is no availability SLA, and practitioners are pricing the move in tail latency and operational toil.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/qconlondon-2027-track/en/headerimage/qcon-london-2027-track-focus-1790854597434.jpg"/><p>A preview of the 15-track QCon London 2027 program, covering agent evaluation and guardrails, AI-era architecture, distributed-system debugging, modern data platforms, high-performance engineering, and Staff+ leadership.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

item.title: Presentation: Building Resilient Platforms: Insights from 20+ Years in Mission-Critical Infrastructure
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/infrastructure-financial-services-platform/en/mediumimage/medium-1790844962852.jpeg"/><p>Matthew Liste explains the 12 core principles of building scalable, reliable platforms for enterprise tech teams. From avoiding technical debt and managing deprecation to building a strong engineering culture, Liste discusses how to design infrastructure platforms that reduce complexity, streamline developer workflows, and deliver long-term value for senior architects and engineering leaders.</p> <i>By Matthew Liste</i>

item.title: Flagged by the Machine: How Google Ads Suspended an Open-Source macOS Term as Malicious
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/google-wrong-flagging/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791090830972.jpg"/><p>Przemyslaw Alexander Kaminski created RACE, a Rust terminal multiplexer on an infinite canvas that detaches child shells into background processes. When he launched an ad campaign, automated scanners suspended his account for malware despite clean notarization and Safe Browsing checks. The flag illustrates operational deadlocks when ad heuristics evaluate POSIX process architectures.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Introduces CLI for AI Agents, Sunsetting Wrangler
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-cf-cli/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790917350141.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently launched the open beta of cf, a new open-source, agent-focused command-line interface for interacting with Cloudflare services through a unified CLI. Written in TypeScript, it provides structured output and command discovery to make Cloudflare’s APIs easier for both developers and AI agents.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

Written in TypeScript, it provides structured output and command discovery to make Cloudflare’s APIs easier for both developers and AI agents.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Java News Roundup: JobRunr 9, OpenXava 8, Quarkus, LangChain4j, JNoSQL, Introducing Lathe
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/java-news-roundup-sep28-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1791219262766.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for September 28th, 2026, features news highlighting: the GA releases of JobRunr 9.0 and OpenXava 8.0; point releases for Quarkus, Micronaut, LangChain4j, Eclipse JNoSQL; ADK for Java and ADK for Kotlin; and introducing Lathe, a new Java language server.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

item.title: Akka Tests Spec-Driven AI Delivery across 65 Open Source Projects
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-spec-driven-delivery/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789859037002.jpg"/><p>Akka used 65 open-source projects to examine how specification structure, context, model selection, automated validation, and delivery guardrails affect AI assisted software porting. The experiment measured time, token use, code size, test parity, and performance, finding substantial variation across models, effort levels, and project types.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Podcast: Future Cybersecurity: Hardware Memory Safety, Automated Governance and Post-Quantum Cryptography
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/future-cybersecurity-hardware-memory-safety/en/smallimage/infoq-podcast-500-1790672981256.jpg"/><p>In this episode, Chris Swan, engineer at Atsign and security track host at QCon London, reflects on the ideas shared during QCon London 2026 and teases topics of the future edition. The discussion explores how security engineering is shifting from relying on human vigilance toward automated, system-level defences across the entire application stack.</p> <i>By Chris Swan</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Fixes Cross-Tenant Data Exposure in Containers
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-cross-tenant-exposure/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790844732167.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has disclosed a cross-tenant data exposure vulnerability in Containers and Sandboxes, caused by thin-provisioned storage pools configured to skip zeroing reused blocks. Researchers recovered directory structures, database pages and complete SQLite databases across four continents. Cloudflare remediated it and found no evidence of exploitation.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Plans Public Certificate Authority to Issue Quantum-Safe TLS Certificates
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/postquatam-certificates/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791007674738.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare will operate a free public Certificate Authority to issue quantum-safe Transport Layer Security certificates. This initiative addresses challenges in migrating from classical public key cryptography to post-quantum methods. It utilizes Merkle Tree Certificates to reduce data payloads and maintain system efficiency, while also enhancing certificate transparency and revocation processes.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: GitLab Vulnerability under Active Exploitation Enables Unauthenticated Data Exfiltration
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gitlab-critical-vulnerabilities/en/headerimage/gitlab-cloud-seed-preview-1791042234130.jpeg"/><p>CVE-2026-85706 is a critical GitLab path-traversal vulnerability that has moved beyond theoretical risk into confirmed exploitation. It affects self-managed GitLab CE/EE and could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to read arbitrary files from the GitLab.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Presentation: Building GenAI Platform at DoorDash
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/doordash-genai-platform-architecture/en/mediumimage/SiddharthKodwaniSwaroopChitlur-medium-1790246592519.jpg"/><p>Swaroop Chitlur and Sidd Kodwani share DoorDash’s journey building an internal GenAI platform. They discuss core architectural bets, transitioning from vendor-first setups to open-weights models, navigating LLM and agent gateways, and balancing accuracy, latency, and cost for over 5,000 internal users.</p> <i>By Siddharth Kodwani, Swaroop Chitlur</i>

item.title: Istio 1.31 Adds Agentgateway Waypoints and Moves Release Artifacts off Google Cloud
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/istio-1-31-agentgateway/en/headerimage/header-1790887193946.jpeg"/><p>Istio 1.31 adds agentgateway waypoints in ambient mode, with a canary configuration fix included in 1.31.1. It also ends the publication of images and Helm charts to Google Cloud, requiring repository migration ahead of the 13 October outage test and signing-key updates for teams verifying images.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: Envoy Gateway 1.9.1 Tightens Security and Addresses a Difficult Upgrade Path
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/envoy-gateway-1-9-1/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790172096430.jpg"/><p>Envoy Gateway has released v1.9.1, a maintenance release that focuses heavily on security, upgrade reliability, and operational correctness following the broader v1.9 release.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: Managing Asynchronous APIs at Scale
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/managing-async-apis/en/mediumimage/ian-cooper-medium-1790242149604.jpeg"/><p>Ian Cooper discusses managing asynchronous APIs in event-driven architectures at scale. He explains the "ABCs" of messaging (Address, Binding, Contract) and shares how to tackle discovery, governance, and provisioning using AsyncAPI, CloudEvents, schema registries, and automated CI/CD infrastructure pipelines based on real-world engineering practices at Just Eat Takeaway.</p> <i>By Ian Cooper</i>

item.title: DigitalOcean Managed Agents Brings Managed Cloud Infrastructure to AI Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/digitalocean-managed-agents/en/headerimage/digitalocean-managed-agents-1790930999544.jpeg"/><p>DigitalOcean recently launched DigitalOcean Managed Agents in public preview, offering a managed cloud infrastructure layer for AI agents with isolated microVM runtimes, governed tool access, and serverless AI inference.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Article: From Reusable to Regeneratable: Rethinking the Shared UI Component Library
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/regeneratable-ui-component-library/en/headerimage/regeneratable-ui-component-library-header-1790758478325.jpg"/><p>Regeneration has changed reuse economics. A model pointed at a solid design system can produce most standard UI on demand, so paying to keep a canonical component package alive is much harder to justify than it used to be. Keep the design system, tokens, guidelines and tests central. They are what actually buy you consistency.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Presentation: Beyond Observability: Evolving Production Operations in the Age of AI
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-production-operations/en/mediumimage/infoq-live-medium-1790856304338.jpg"/><p>The panelists discuss how production operations are evolving with AI, turning operational data into actionable insights for incident response. They explain how automation and new architectural practices help engineering teams build more understandable systems, while exploring how AI reshapes software delivery and changes the historically deterministic nature of production applications.</p> <i>By Michael Hausenblas, Sujana Sooreddy, Noam Levi, Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Article: High Availability is Not Resilience: Why Cloud Systems Fail When it Matters Most
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/high-availability-not-resilience-cloud/en/headerimage/high-availability-not-resilience-cloud-header-1790670587417.jpg"/><p>A routine TLS 1.3 upgrade silently broke Route 53 health checks, causing a CDN to stop routing traffic to a healthy region while internal dashboards showed nothing wrong. This article examines why HA and resilience are different problems, how control-plane dependencies create invisible failure modes, and why recovery capability erodes without explicit ownership.</p> <i>By Alexey Golev</i>

item.title: SvelteKit 3 Reaches Release Candidate, Moving Config to Vite and Retiring the $lib Alias
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/sveltekit-3-vite/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790668846660.jpg"/><p>The Svelte team has entered the release candidate phase for SvelteKit 3, which focuses on code refinement and prepares for future updates. Notable changes include moving configuration to vite.config.ts, replacing the $lib alias with #lib for improved compatibility. SvelteKit 3 requires Vite 8 and Svelte 5, enhancing error handling and build efficiency, while retaining some experimental features.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Vercel Labs Ships scriptc, a TypeScript-to-Native Compiler That Leaves the JavaScript Engine behind
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/vercel-scriptc-node/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790243494065.jpg"/><p>Vercel Labs has introduced scriptc, an experimental compiler that converts TypeScript into small native executables without relying on Node, V8, or a JavaScript engine. It uses the TypeScript compiler for type checking and can output C or WebAssembly code. Initial benchmarks show faster startup times and lower memory usage than Node, though it experiences slower execution speeds.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Canvas UI Ships 35 HTML-in-Canvas Components That Run WebGL and WebGPU Effects over Live DOM
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/canvas-ui-webgl/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790080690608.jpg"/><p>Canvas UI is an open-source component library created by David Haz, utilizing the experimental HTML-in-Canvas API. It features 35 components that render GPU effects on live page content while maintaining accessibility. The library integrates with multiple frameworks and requires specific Chrome versions for full functionality.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Changesets v3: Bumps Peer Dependents by Patch and Ships ESM Only with an 88% Smaller Install
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/changesets-v3-release/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789995898981.jpg"/><p>Changesets v3.0, released on August 11, 2026, introduces significant updates for JavaScript monorepos. It offers leaner installations, a rebuilt CLI, and changes to peer dependency management that resolve long-standing complaints. Upgrading involves configuration updates. The tool focuses on versioning and changelogs while supporting contributors in declaring release intents.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
